referents.why: First-person singular 'me' in the psalm's own voice; the psalm quotes no one here, so the voice candidate fits.
Same first-person singular 'me' in the second line, in the psalm's own voice.

Third masculine singular implied subject of the yiqtol 'makes me lie down'. The shepherd of verse 1 is the LORD, and making a flock lie down is a shepherd's act, so the nearest agreeing sensible doer is the LORD. David agrees in morphology but does not fit the act as the verse frames it.
Third masculine singular implied subject of the yiqtol 'leads me'. The same shepherd subject carries across the parallel line.

groups.why: Two poetic lines of one verse. The second restates the first's roles (me, a place of rest) with the subject the same and unstated: the LORD of verse 1.
groups.category: parallel lines with implied shared subject
